messages:
sam: Heads up — seeing goroutines hang in the Go client when cancelling streaming requests over HTTP/2. ctx gets canceled but the stream goroutine doesn't exit; leaks until transport idle timeout. Anyone seen this?

jia: Yep, saw something similar last week. Context is propagated to the Request, but http2 stream cancellation sometimes stalls if we're reusing the conn. Can you paste your transport config and how you cancel?

sam: Here's the relevant bits:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  ForceAttemptHTTP2: true,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  ResponseHeaderTimeout: 0,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
// cancel via cancel() on ctx
```

omar: Two quick things: set ResponseHeaderTimeout (non-zero) and maybe lower MaxIdleConnsPerHost for debugging. For streaming keepalives + http2, IdleConnTimeout matters. Are you using net/http's built-in http2 or x/net/http2.Transport?

sam: Using default net/http with ForceAttemptHTTP2; no custom x/net/http2 usage.

jia: Try this: Request.Cancel is deprecated so it won't help. Also set TLSHandshakeTimeout and ResponseHeaderTimeout; but for stream-cancel leaks we've been using an explicit close of resp.Body in the cancel handler to force the client to release the stream: 
```go
go func() {
  <-ctx.Done()
  if resp != nil {
    resp.Body.Close()
  }
}()
```

maria: Also check server behavior — if the server doesn't ack RST_STREAM the client may wait until connection-level pings or idle timeout. Do you have server logs to confirm it sent an RST?

sam: We do. Server logs show it sends RST on cancel but the client-side goroutine stays in a write loop. Using httptrace, I saw the conn is reused and frames back up — looks like write is blocked by flow control.

mark: We had something similar in runtime; one workaround was setting a per-connection write deadline when closing to avoid stuck writes: 
```go
if nc, ok := rw.(net.Conn); ok {
  nc.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
}
```
Not ideal but can break the deadlock.

jia: FWIW we documented transport tuning: increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost and IdleConnTimeout to reduce dial churn. But for cancel leaks we found the pragmatic fix was explicit resp.Body.Close in the cancel path. If you want to go deeper, switching to x/net/http2.Transport gives you more control (Framer) but it's invasive.

omar: For retries: only retry idempotent ops and respect ctx deadlines. Our helper in pkg/retry uses exponential backoff and checks ctx.Err() before each attempt — important for streaming endpoints where partial writes leave the connection in a weird state.

sam: Thanks — I'll try adding explicit resp.Body.Close on cancel + set ResponseHeaderTimeout and a small write deadline around close, then reproduce. Will post repro logs here. Ping @mark for a quick review if I open a small client change.

sam: :thumbsup: Thanks all. I'll upload the repro and trace output once I have it.
